tasks.issue_text:
A method decorated with cachetools' @cachedmethod does not behave like a plain method when it is called through the class and the instance is passed by keyword.
Expected: Cached.get(self=obj, value=1) gives the same result as Cached.get(obj, value=1) when the method's first parameter is really called `self`, and the method is only computed once per distinct argument. If the first parameter has another name (for example `this`), then Named.get(this=obj, value=1) works but Named.get(self=obj, value=1) must raise TypeError, exactly as a plain function would. A positional-only first parameter must not accept the instance by keyword (TypeError). Calling the method through the class with no instance at all (Cached.get(value=1)), or a decorated method that takes no parameters (Named.get_noargs()), must raise TypeError.
Calls through an instance must keep working and keep caching as before.

Stacking cachetools caching decorators does not work as it should. If a function that is already wrapped by cachetools.cached(...) (or by one of the decorators in cachetools.func such as lru_cache) is wrapped a second time with its own cache, the two layers must stay independent.
Expected: the outer wrapper's __wrapped__ is the inner wrapper; the outer wrapper has its own cache (outer.cache is the cache passed to the outer decorator), its own cache_info() counters, cache_parameters() and cache_clear(); clearing the outer cache does not clear the inner one; the inner wrapper keeps its own hit/miss counts and parameters. For example with two info=True layers, calling outer(0) twice gives outer.cache_info() == (1, 1, 2, 1) and inner.cache_info() == (0, 1, 2, 1).
Today these expectations do not hold when two cachetools decorators are stacked.

RRCache.popitem() on an empty cache must raise KeyError, whatever `choice` function the cache was created with. The documented contract only requires `choice` to handle non-empty sequences (for example choice=min, choice=max, or lambda seq: next(iter(seq))), but with such a function an empty cache currently raises some other exception instead of KeyError.
Expected: popitem() on an empty RRCache raises KeyError; after adding one item popitem() returns that item and the next popitem() raises KeyError again. The default random.choice behaviour must stay the same.

click.utils.make_default_short_help(help, max_length) cuts the help text at the end of the first sentence if it fits, but it mistakes abbreviations and other dots for the end of a sentence.
Expected results: ("123 567 9. Aaaa bbb", 10) -> "123 567 9."; ("123 567 9.", 10) -> "123 567 9."; ("Weigh apples vs. pears.", 30) -> "Weigh apples vs. pears." (a dot followed by a lowercase word is not a sentence end); ("Weigh apples vs. pears and plums.", 20) -> "Weigh apples vs...."; ("123 567 9. aaaa bbb", 10) -> "123 567..."; ("Pick a fruit. 3 remain.", 20) -> "Pick a fruit.". A hyphenated word or one long word is never split: ("well-behaved.", 8) -> "...", ("supercalifragilistic", 10) -> "...". When max_length is too small for the "..." suffix (3 or less, or negative) the result is just "..."; text that already fits ("ab", 2) is returned unchanged.

more_itertools.peekable slicing with a negative step and an omitted stop reads and caches the whole underlying iterable, even though only the items down to the start index are needed.
Expected: for p = peekable(iter(range(100))), p[5::-1] returns [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0], and afterwards only 6 items have been pulled from the source (len(p._cache) == 6) and next(p) still returns 0. A peekable over an infinite iterator such as itertools.count() must also support this: p[4::-2] returns [4, 2, 0] without hanging, with 5 items cached, and next(p) still returns 0.
Other slicing behaviour must not change.

chunked_even(iterable, n) mishandles edge chunk sizes.
With n=0 it raises an internal islice error instead of yielding nothing, and it consumes items from the source iterator first.
With negative n it leaks a low-level islice index error instead of a clear ValueError, and also touches the source.
It should reject n<0 with a ValueError without reading the source, and treat n=0 as empty output.

packaging.licenses.canonicalize_license_expression mangles LicenseRef identifiers that differ only in letter case. The idstring after "LicenseRef-" is case-insensitive in SPDX, so spellings that differ only in case are the same license and the result must use one spelling for all of them: the first spelling that appears in the expression.
Expected: "LicenseRef-mit OR licenseref-MIT" -> "LicenseRef-mit OR LicenseRef-mit"; "licenseref-MIT AND LicenseRef-mit" -> "LicenseRef-MIT AND LicenseRef-MIT"; "(LICENSEREF-Foo OR licenseref-foo) AND MIT AND LicenseRef-FOO" -> "(LicenseRef-Foo OR LicenseRef-Foo) AND MIT AND LicenseRef-Foo"; "licenseref-public-domain" -> "LicenseRef-public-domain". Expressions without case-variant LicenseRef identifiers must give the same result as today.

packaging.requirements.Requirement accepts a URL that contains a line break. For example Requirement("name @ https://example.com/name.whl\nevil==1") (also with \r and \r\n) is parsed with the rest of the text absorbed into the URL, so serializing the requirement later could produce a second requirement line.
Expected: a requirement whose URL contains whitespace such as a line break must be rejected with InvalidRequirement. Ordinary URL requirements such as "name @ https://example.com/name.whl" must keep parsing.

packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename silently accepts a malformed build tag that contains a newline. For example "foo-1.0-1
abc-py3-none-any.whl" returns build=(1, '') and drops the rest of the build part without raising.
Expected: a build part must match the build tag format in full; a build part such as "1
abc" or "1
" must raise InvalidWheelFilename. Valid build tags such as "1" or "1abc" must keep working.

semver.Version.replace() hides the real error when the new value for a version part has the wrong type. For example Version.parse("1.2.3").replace(major=None) (or minor/patch set to None or a plain object()) fails in the Version constructor with a TypeError that says what is wrong, but replace() raises a different, less useful error message instead.
Expected: when the keyword names are valid, replace() raises the same TypeError, with the identical message, that Version(**parts) would raise for those values. The existing custom error for genuinely unknown keyword names must stay as it is, and replace() on subclasses must keep working.

dateutil.relativedelta(yearday=366) resolves to the wrong day in leap years: it gives December 30, the same date as yearday=365.
Expected: for every year, date(year, 1, 1) + relativedelta(yearday=n) is the n-th day of that year, for n from 1 to 365 in common years and 1 to 366 in leap years (so yearday=366 is December 31 in a leap year), checked for years such as 1900, 2000, 2001 and 2024. Other yeardays must keep their current results.

humanize.naturaldelta truncates the number of years instead of rounding it to the nearest year. A timedelta of 2.6 years (365 * 2.6 days) is shown as "2 years" but should be "3 years".
Expected: days=365*2 -> "2 years"; 365*2.4 -> "2 years"; 365*2.6 -> "3 years"; 365*2.9 -> "3 years"; 365*3 -> "3 years". Results below one year must not change.

tasks.issue_text:
dateutil.tz.tzfile reads the POSIX TZ string at the end of a compiled zone file (the footer) to work out the daylight-saving transitions after the last explicit transition. The day-of-year rules in such strings give the wrong dates.
Rule "n" counts days from 0 (0..365) and does count February 29th in leap years. It currently comes out one day early: with the footer "STD0DST-1,10/0,J100/0" the DST period should start on January 11th (day 10 counted from 0), not January 10th; "STD0DST-1,59/0,300/0" starts DST on February 29th in a leap year (2024) and on March 1st otherwise (2023). A rule "0/0" must not land on December 31st of the previous year.
Rule "Jn" counts from 1 (1..365) and never counts February 29th: J59 is always February 28th, and J60 is always March 1st, also in leap years (so with "STD0DST-1,J60/0,J300/0" in 2024 February 29th is still standard time and DST starts on March 1st). Today the leap-year shift starts one day too early, at J59.
A zone that is on DST all year, written like "EST5EDT,0/0,J365/25" or "<+00>0<+01>,0/0,J365/25", must really be on DST across New Year as well.
The "Mm.w.d" rules must keep giving the dates they give now.

semver.Version.next_version("prerelease", token) can return a version that is OLDER than the one it was called on, when you switch to a prerelease token that sorts earlier than the current one. The result must always be greater than the original.
Expected: switching to an earlier-sorting token moves to the next patch version and restarts the counter: "1.2.3-rc.1" with token "alpha" -> "1.2.4-alpha.1"; "1.2.3-beta.3" + "alpha" -> "1.2.4-alpha.1"; "1.2.3-rc.1+build.7" + "dev" -> "1.2.4-dev.1" (build metadata is dropped); "1.2.3-rc3" + "alpha" -> "1.2.4-alpha.1"; "1.2.3-rc.1" + "2" -> "1.2.4-2.1"; "1.2.3-alphaXbeta9" + "alpha.beta" -> "1.2.4-alpha.beta.1".
Switching to a token that sorts later keeps the patch version: "1.2.3-alpha.4" + "rc" -> "1.2.3-rc.1". Incrementing with the same token behaves as before. The original Version object is never modified.

Instances of a class that has @cachedmethod methods can no longer be pickled; pickle.dumps(obj) fails. This worked in earlier releases and must work again (issue 417), for methods decorated with plain @cachedmethod(cachefn) and with info=True, and for a subclass that adds its own cached method.
Expected: pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(obj)) returns an object whose cached methods work and use the cache that the cache function returns for the unpickled object. The cache contents travel with the object: if obj's cache held one entry when it was pickled, the unpickled object's cache holds that entry too (a hit on it is a hit) and further calls fill the unpickled object's cache, not the original's. For info=True methods the hit/miss counters start again at 0 after unpickling, while currsize reflects the cache contents (e.g. cache_info() == (0, 0, maxsize, 1) right after unpickling an object whose cache holds one entry).
Normal (non-pickled) behaviour must not change.
